hook.line: SEO is not technical, and that includes GEO and AI SEO.
hook.visual: Walk-and-talk selfie of a man in glasses on a sunny desert street, orange title 'Do you need to rebuild your website for AI?' on top, big word-by-word caption below.

beats.what: Contrarian claim plus the title question: do you need to rebuild your site for AI?
Sets up the client request he hears weekly: 'rebuild our website for AI'
Cut; promises to separate 'making your site usable by AI' from 'what helps you get recommended'
Explains fan-out queries: AI searches an index, picks trusted pages, retrieves passages
Cut; 'That's all AI search does': not llms.txt, not structured data, not WebMCP
Cut; his agency's split: 70% content, 30% authority building
Cut; the future: AI agents will fill forms and use tools on your site
Cut; what to do today: add an llms.txt page and WebMCP tags on forms
Cut; caveat: structure your site for AI so you can update it with AI, not for traffic

why_it_works: Contrarian opener ('SEO is not technical') against a popular fear (rebuild your site for AI) makes viewers stay to see if he is right
Explains the actual mechanism (fan-out queries, retrieval of passages) in plain words, which earns trust for the advice
Myth-busting list (not llms.txt, not structured data, not WebMCP) then a short 'do these two things today' list gives a clear takeaway
Big word-by-word captions with the active word in an orange box carry the message for muted viewers on a plain walk-and-talk
weaknesses: 168 s long with one 51.6 s shot and no visuals; the fan-out explanation would land faster as a diagram
Seems to contradict itself: llms.txt is said to be ignored, then recommended as one of two things to do
Captions sit at the very bottom, almost entirely outside the safe area
for_robert: Use the myth-vs-mechanism structure, but draw the fan-out process: Fred could swim through a row of pages and bring back one passage, showing what he only describes in words.
